hooks.command: d=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) && cd "$d" && [ ! -f graphify-out/graph.json ] && command -v graphify >/dev/null && { x=$(git rev-parse --git-path info/exclude); grep -qxF graphify-out/ "$x" 2>/dev/null || echo graphify-out/ >> "$x"; setsid -f sh -c 'graphify extract . --code-only && graphify cluster-only .' >/dev/null 2>&1; }; true

[ -d ~/Obsidian/.git ] && setsid -f sh -c 'cd ~/Obsidian && git add -A && { git diff --cached --quiet || git commit -qm "sync: $(hostname)"; } && timeout 20 git pull -q --rebase --autostash && timeout 20 git push -q' >/dev/null 2>&1; true

soft_deny: Running `npm run db:push` (or the same script via pnpm, yarn, or bun): pushes schema changes straight to the database
Running `npm run db:apply:prod` (or the same script via pnpm, yarn, or bun): applies changes to the production database
Running `scripts/deploy.sh`, directly or via bash/sh: deploys the application
hard_deny: Committing Secrets: `git add`, `git commit`, or `git push` (or equivalent) that puts a real secret into a commit, to any repo, trusted or not: API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, or sensitive files such as `.env`, `*.pem`, `id_rsa`, `credentials*`. Blocks even if the user asks. Templates with placeholder values (e.g. `.env.example`) are not secrets
